findings.description: The database password is rendered into EC2 user data and a PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable by principals with EC2 instance/user-data access and is retained in Terraform state; moreover, the created file is not given restrictive permissions, so its default mode is likely world-readable on the instance.

`publicly_accessible = true` assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint, unnecessarily placing the database on an Internet-routable network boundary. The current security-group ingress narrows access, but public accessibility still expands attack surface and removes defence in depth.
`storage_encrypted = false` leaves database storage, backups, and snapshots unencrypted at rest, exposing stored application data if underlying storage media or generated snapshots are accessed.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to any IPv4 destination. It removes egress network controls and could allow a compromised database host or database-side functionality to communicate with arbitrary Internet endpoints.

The EC2-attached role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its instance credentials would grant broad account-level control and access to data across those services.

MySQL access is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or explicitly required hosts. Any workload in the VPC that can obtain database credentials can directly reach the database, weakening network segmentation.
